title: Isolate continuous-batcher driver, add KV-lease shim, modernize concurrency deps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The continuous batching subsystem and KV cache ownership are currently intertwined in the batch driver and prefetch threads. This coupling causes difficult-to-reproduce stalls during heavy burst traffic and complicates recent concurrency library upgrades. Goal: split the continuous-batcher driver into a lightweight coordinator that only handles admission/commit semantics and a separate execution driver responsible for prefetch and KV interactions. Introduce a thin KV-lease shim that serializes lease handoff and exposes a compact API for warmup/eviction operations. While doing this, upgrade the coroutine/concurrency deps (task scheduler, futures lib) to the latest LTS release and remove legacy locking primitives. Expected wins: improved tail latency under burst, simpler reasoning about KV owner lifetimes, fewer global locks, and fewer hotpaths during scale-up/scale-down transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator and execution driver are separate modules with a clear public API and unit tests
KV-lease shim implements lease acquire/release, heartbeat, and safe-evict hooks documented in README
No increase in median token latency and reduced 95th/99th percentile tail by >= 10% in the synthetic burst benchmark
All existing integration tests remain green after concurrency dep upgrade
No new global locks introduced; code uses the new task scheduler primitives for async work
tasks: Design API for coordinator <-> execution driver and write design brief
Implement coordinator skeleton and move admission logic into it
Implement KV-lease shim and replace direct lease manipulation sites
Port prefetch/warmup code to use KV-lease shim and new async primitives
Upgrade concurrency dependency to runtime-concurrency-3.2.0 and resolve compile errors
Add unit and integration tests for shim and driver interactions
Develop synthetic burst benchmark and run before/after comparison
Prepare rollout plan with canary and fallback to previous driver
notes: This PR targets the continuous-batcher package and touches hotpaths; keep diffs small and review-focused
We should not change public API shapes consumed by Dedicated/Private agents in this change window; add adapter layer if needed
Consider a feature flag to toggle use of the KV-lease shim for quicker rollbacks
Heap and allocation profiles need to be captured before changes to ensure we don't regress memory usage
